SELF_REVIEW:
- TDD (I01, I04): RED first. `generate_manifest_skips_an_entry_with_a_missing_skill_file` failed before the fix (`assertion left == 2 right == 1`), then passed after `generate_manifest` switched to `skill.is_failed()`. Field removal was then driven by compilation and the existing suite.
- Tests assert behavior (I02, I03): the new test drives the public `generate_manifest` with an entry whose directory resolves but whose root `SKILL.md` is missing; no mocks, no private helpers. Existing tests were only updated where they read the retired field.
- AC coverage (I05, I22) — each AC has executed evidence:
  - AC1 (no directory-level status): `ExpectedSetEntry` no longer has a `resolution` field; `cargo test -p skill-index` (22 passed) and `cargo test --workspace` compile and pass with all reads routed through `is_failed()` / `SkillFile::resolution`. `grep` shows no `entry.resolution` reads left anywhere.
  - AC2 (messages keep location + reason): `pack_fails_on_missing_vendor_entry` now asserts the error names the skill, the literal `vendor skill directory not found`, and the missing absolute path; `validation` tests assert `<source> skill directory not found` for upstream/vendor/autopilot missing directories. Dev wording is unchanged: `missing_skill_files` still renders the same `SkillFile` reasons (the only failure vocabulary now). All pass.
  - AC3 (compile + workspace green + lint): `cargo test --workspace` → 335 passed, 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` → exit 0.
  - AC4 (behavior preserved): dev policy, pack strictness (`reject_failed_entries` runs before staging/manifest), tarball/installed layout, lock format and entry-state verdicts untouched; all pre-existing suites green. One library-level deliberate change, see Risk below.
  - AC5 (suites are referee): no assertions relaxed. Additions only: one new manifest test, three extra `pack` message assertions, and the entry-level assertions replaced by equivalent `is_failed()` / root-`SkillFile` assertions.
- Risk / API contract (I32): every caller and doc was updated. Only remaining entry-level API is the derived `is_failed()`; no consumer reads a retired status. `ResolutionStatus` doc now describes a Skill file, and `CONTEXT.md`'s Expected-set entry definition no longer claims a directory-level resolved status.
- Risk / behavior preservation (I33): deliberate behavior change — `generate_manifest` now also skips entries that own a missing variant file, not just missing directories. This path is unreachable through `pack` (it calls `reject_failed_entries` first and bails), so shipped tarball behavior is identical; the change is required because there is no other failure source to consult.
- Context (I06–I09, I30): read the issue contract, `CONTEXT.md`, ADR 0045, the sibling modules in the plan (`crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs`, `crates/deploy/src/pack.rs`, `crates/deploy/src/dev.rs`, `crates/validation-runner/src/lib.rs`, `tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs`), and `docs/adr/0044` for the historical baseline. Stayed inside the named seam; no new dependencies; no scope creep.
- Diagnosis (I16, I25, I26): no blocking fact, no ambiguity; not applicable.
- Full-suite run (I17): `cargo test --workspace` → 335 passed, 0 failed. Also ran `rust-script --test tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs` (1 passed), `rust-script --test tests/test_install.rs` (7 passed), `rust-script scripts/check.rs` (ALL PASS), `rust-script validation/run.rs` (All skills PASS validation). Pre-existing note: in earlier baseline runs `distill-cli`'s `transition::tests::worktree_projection_bytes_do_not_count_against_quota` flaked under parallel load (`injected state write failure for run-1`, crates/distill-cli/src/transition.rs:167) and passed when run alone; it passed in the final full run and is unrelated to this change.
- Formatting (I29): edited Rust files are `rustfmt --check` clean. Repo-wide `cargo fmt --all --check` reports pre-existing drift in untouched files (e.g. crates/distill-cli/src/*.rs, crates/deploy/src/lib.rs, crates/git-utils/src/lib.rs); not introduced here and not mass-reformatted to avoid unrelated churn.
- No issues found that required a fix during self-review.
CHANGED_FILES:
- crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs — removed `ExpectedSetEntry::resolution` and its constructor wiring; `generate_manifest` skips any entry with a missing Skill file; file-level `ResolutionStatus` docs; new RED-first manifest test plus tests updated to `is_failed()` / root `SkillFile` resolution.
- crates/validation-runner/src/lib.rs — removed the retired entry-level field from the `test_entry` fixture helper (production code already read `target.file.resolution`).
- crates/deploy/src/pack.rs — strengthened `pack_fails_on_missing_vendor_entry` to assert the missing skill name, the `vendor skill directory not found` reason, and the missing path; production behavior unchanged.
- CONTEXT.md — Expected-set entry definition now describes the Skill files it owns instead of a directory-level resolved status.
- docs/adr/0045-expected-set-entry-resolves-its-skill-files.md (pre-existing) — design source for the change; read, not edited.
- crates/deploy/src/dev.rs (pre-existing) — already derived failure from `skill_files`; warning wording unchanged, no edit needed.
- crates/validation-runner/src/lib.rs (production paths pre-existing) — `build_validation_targets` / `validate_all` / `check_codex_status` already read file-level resolution; only the test helper was edited.
- tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs (pre-existing) — already consumes `entry.is_failed()` and `file.resolution`; ran green unchanged.
- corpus/issue-126.json (pre-existing, plan context; not present in this worktree) — issue contract source.
- corpus/issue-121.json (pre-existing, plan context; not present in this worktree) — parent spec source.
SUMMARY: Retired the entry-level resolution status so an Expected-set entry's failure vocabulary is only the Skill files it owns, while dev/pack/validation keep naming the same missing locations and reasons and all suites stay green.
